visual: Classic hardy waterlily with rounded green floating leaves, often bronze-flushed when young, and large semi-double flowers that open cream-white to very pale blush pink with a warm golden-yellow centre.
water: Permanent still water; aim for about 45–75cm of water over the crown once established, starting shallower while establishing.
soil: Heavy aquatic loam; Not multipurpose; it floats out
prune: Remove fading flowers and yellow or damaged leaves regularly. Cut dying foliage back low in late autumn before it sinks and decays.
resilience: Hardy, vigorous and long-lived in stable still water; generally low maintenance once established but dislikes constant splashing and overcrowding.
uses: Medium to large ponds, wildlife ponds, ornamental aquatic planting, water-surface cover and summer flowering.

soil: Fertile, well-drained
prune: After flowering, can be hard pruned

visual: Glossy evergreen leaves, fragrant white star flowers · early spring
soil: Fertile, well-drained
prune: After flowering if needed

visual: Vigorous twiner, frothy white flower sprays · summer/autumn
soil: Any, even poor
prune: Hard prune to control

visual: Distinctive rosette-forming herbaceous perennial with upright, softly hairy, spear-shaped pale green leaves and erect flower stems topped by narrow conical spikes. The flowers open progressively from the base as vivid lilac to pinkish-purple blooms beneath a striking cap of unopened crimson-red buds, creating a miniature red-hot-poker effect.
water: Keep consistently moist through the growing season; water in dry spells and never let it dry out for long. Sun is only safe where moisture is reliable.
aspect: Best in partial shade on a sheltered north-, east- or west-facing aspect. It tolerates brighter and even sunny positions in cool conditions provided the soil remains consistently moist.
soil: Deep humus-rich loam, acid; Avoid winter waterlogging
prune: Cut spent flowering stems back after flowering. Remove dead foliage as it collapses, and divide established clumps after flowering where rejuvenation or propagation is required.
resilience: Cold-hardy but somewhat less persistent than its hardiness rating suggests. Often relatively short-lived in cultivation and performs best where summers remain cool and the soil stays moist without becoming waterlogged in winter. It may self-seed where conditions suit it.
uses: Excellent for damp woodland borders, shady herbaceous borders, pond and stream margins, moist rock gardens and mass planting.

visual: Spectacular architectural shrub or small tree forming upright stems topped by enormous deeply lobed green leaves, often 60cm or more across and capable of approaching 1m in favourable conditions.
water: Water regularly while establishing and during prolonged dry spells.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist; Suckers widely; avoid winter wet
prune: Remove frost-damaged or unwanted stems in spring once new growth is visible. Unwanted suckers should be removed promptly if spread needs restricting.
resilience: Extremely vigorous once established in favourable conditions and capable of recovering strongly after frost damage, but the top growth is vulnerable to severe winter cold and exposed winds.
uses: Exotic gardens, architectural planting, jungle-style borders, sheltered courtyards and dramatic foliage displays.

visual: Ancient-looking evergreen tree fern with a thick fibrous brown trunk supporting a broad crown of gracefully arching, finely divided deep green fronds that can eventually reach around 2m or more in length.
water: Keep the fibrous trunk and root zone consistently moist through the growing season, particularly in warm dry weather.
soil: Humus-rich, moist, acid; Never let trunk or roots dry out
prune: Remove old brown fronds close to the trunk once they have died. Do not cut or damage the central growing point.
resilience: Long-lived but extremely slow to form trunk.
uses: Woodland gardens, shaded courtyards, exotic planting, fern gardens, sheltered containers and architectural focal points.

visual: Bold suckering deciduous shrub or small tree with thick spreading branches and distinctive reddish-brown young stems covered in velvety hairs.
water: Water while establishing; mature plants are reasonably drought tolerant once rooted and usually need supplementary watering only during prolonged dryness.
soil: Any, well-drained; Suckers metres from the parent plant
prune: Little routine pruning is required. Remove unwanted suckers at their point of origin and remove damaged or badly placed stems during dormancy.
resilience: Extremely tough, hardy and adaptable, with strong regenerative ability from its spreading root system.
uses: Autumn-colour planting, large shrub borders, wildlife gardens, informal screens, banks and specimen planting where root spread can be accommodated.

visual: Compact clump-forming perennial with large glossy, strongly veined leaflets opening vivid reddish bronze in spring, becoming darker green through summer and colouring again in autumn.
water: Keep consistently moist throughout spring and summer.
soil: Deep, fertile, moist; Dry or hot sites scorch the foliage
prune: Remove spent flower stems after flowering if desired and cut dead foliage to ground level after it collapses in autumn.
resilience: Long-lived and dependable in consistently moist ground, but substantially less resilient to drought and hot dry exposure.
uses: Moist borders, woodland edges, pond margins, bog gardens and bold foliage planting.

visual: Bushy deciduous Knap Hill-type azalea producing rounded trusses packed with vivid rose-pink semi-double hose-in-hose flowers in late spring, followed later by attractive autumn foliage colour.
water: Keep evenly moist, particularly during establishment and while flower buds are developing.
soil: Humus-rich, ericaceous; No chalk or lime; keep evenly moist
prune: Little pruning is needed. Remove dead, damaged or badly placed wood after flowering and deadhead young plants if desired.
resilience: Reliable and hardy where soil acidity and moisture are suitable; poor performance is most often associated with alkaline soil, drought or waterlogging.
uses: Woodland gardens, acid borders, spring displays, mixed shrub borders and large ericaceous containers.

visual: Bushy deciduous azalea with green oblong leaves that develop orange and red autumn colour.
water: Maintain even moisture during establishment and dry weather, preferably using rainwater in hard-water districts.
soil: Moist, ericaceous; No chalk; contain — do not let it seed out
prune: Normally requires little pruning beyond removing dead, damaged or badly placed branches after flowering.
resilience: Hardy and vigorous in suitable acidic soil and capable of naturalising where conditions suit it, which is also the reason containment is important.
uses: Contained acid borders, woodland gardens and fragrant spring displays; unsuitable for planting where escape into semi-natural habitats is possible.

visual: Hardy evergreen palm forming a stout solitary trunk wrapped in coarse brown fibres and topped by a crown of large dark green fan-shaped leaves.
soil: Fertile, well-drained; Shelter from wind or leaves shred
prune: Remove only fully brown or damaged lower fronds, cutting cleanly close to the trunk without damaging living tissue.
resilience: Exceptionally cold tolerant for a palm and adaptable to a broad range of UK soils, though leaf quality declines in severe wind exposure.
uses: Exotic gardens, architectural specimen planting, courtyards, urban gardens and large containers while young.

visual: Compact bushy evergreen palm usually forming several stems and a dense rounded crown of stiff green fan-shaped leaves.
water: Water regularly while establishing, then allow the upper soil to dry somewhat between waterings.
soil: Free-draining, fertile; Sharp winter drainage; spiny leaf stalks
prune: Remove completely dead fronds as required. Do not cut into the central growing points.
resilience: Wind, drought and coastal conditions are generally well tolerated once established, but prolonged severe frost and winter wet are the principal risks.
uses: Containers, gravel gardens, courtyards, coastal planting, exotic gardens and architectural displays.

visual: Dramatic evergreen or semi-evergreen subshrub with long blue-grey pinnate leaves made up of sharply toothed leaflets, creating an almost prehistoric silhouette.
water: Provide regular moisture during active growth while allowing good drainage, then keep considerably drier through cold winter weather.
soil: Fertile, sharply drained; Cold wet soil kills; mulch the crown
prune: Remove frost-damaged stems in spring once the extent of dieback is clear. Plants may be cut back hard if winter damage has removed the top growth.
resilience: Fast and vigorous in warm conditions but substantially less tolerant of hard frost and cold wet soil than many architectural shrubs.
uses: Exotic borders, architectural foliage, gravel gardens, large containers and sheltered courtyards.

visual: Bold evergreen perennial forming a substantial clump of long arching sword-shaped leaves with a striking metallic silver sheen.
water: Keep moderately and consistently moist during establishment and dry summer weather, while maintaining free drainage around the crown.
soil: Humus-rich, well-drained; Wet crowns rot in cold winters
prune: Remove individual damaged or dead leaves at the base. Avoid cutting the entire clump back unless frost damage makes renovation necessary.
resilience: Tough in maritime and coastal situations where winters are mild, but significantly less dependable in cold inland gardens or persistently wet soil.
uses: Coastal gardens, architectural containers, modern planting, exotic borders and silver-foliage schemes.

visual: Graceful evergreen clump-forming bamboo with dense slender green culms and masses of narrow fresh-green leaves, creating a soft arching fountain of foliage rather than long invasive running canes.
water: Water regularly during establishment and dry summer weather. Container plants need especially consistent moisture.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist; Clump-forming, but widens with age
prune: Remove dead, weak or badly placed culms at ground level and thin crowded mature clumps where necessary.
resilience: Dependable, hardy and non-running, although drought and exposed drying wind can cause leaf rolling and scorch.
uses: Screening, hedging, containers, Japanese-style planting, evergreen structure and privacy planting.

visual: Tall elegant evergreen bamboo with feathery green foliage and upright culms that emerge green before progressively darkening through brown and purple to glossy near-black as they mature.
water: Water generously during establishment and prolonged dry weather, particularly in containers.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist; Running — needs a rhizome barrier
prune: Remove weak, damaged and older crowded culms at ground level. Thin the lower foliage if the black stems are being grown as a display feature.
resilience: Strong-growing and hardy but potentially troublesome if rhizomes are allowed to escape containment.
uses: Screening, Japanese-style gardens, architectural planting, stem displays and large containers.

visual: Evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy leathery leaves and attractive reddish-brown shredding bark.
water: Water while establishing; mature plants tolerate considerable summer dryness once well rooted.
soil: Well-drained; lime OK; Avoid cold wet heavy ground
prune: Requires little pruning. Remove dead, damaged or badly placed branches in spring and avoid unnecessary hard cutting.
resilience: Evergreen, drought tolerant and notably useful in coastal conditions once established, but dislikes cold waterlogged ground.
uses: Coastal gardens, evergreen specimen planting, wildlife gardens, Mediterranean-style planting and small-tree displays.

visual: Large airy deciduous shrub with slender arching branches clothed in tiny scale-like grey-green leaves, becoming a haze of feathery pink flower panicles from late summer into autumn.
water: Water regularly while establishing; mature plants are drought tolerant and require little supplementary irrigation in normal UK conditions.
soil: Any, reasonably drained; Not shallow chalk; needs an open site
prune: Prune in early spring before new growth, removing old or congested stems and shortening growth where a denser framework is required.
resilience: Excellent tolerance of wind, salt exposure and summer drought once established, making it particularly valuable in difficult coastal gardens.
uses: Coastal planting, large shrub borders, exposed sunny gardens, informal screens and late-summer flowering displays.

visual: Dense evergreen shrub famous for brilliant scarlet-red new foliage that passes through pink and creamy tones before maturing to glossy green.
water: Keep evenly moist, especially when newly planted or container grown. Rainwater is preferable in hard-water districts.
soil: Humus-rich, ericaceous; No chalk; shelter new growth from frost
prune: Normally needs little pruning. Remove spent flower clusters and damaged or badly placed shoots after flowering if required.
resilience: Long-lived in suitable acidic soil but vulnerable to chlorosis on alkaline ground, drought stress and pieris lacebug in some areas.
uses: Ericaceous borders, woodland gardens, spring foliage displays and containers.

visual: Compact evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and dense clusters of deep red flower buds held conspicuously through winter, opening to fragrant creamy-white flowers in early spring.
water: Keep evenly moist and do not allow containers to dry out severely.
soil: Moist, acid to neutral; Alkaline soil and hot sun yellow it
prune: Little pruning is needed. Remove damaged or badly placed growth after flowering.
resilience: Reliable evergreen shrub for shade and containers where moisture is consistent and soil is not strongly alkaline.
uses: Winter containers, shaded borders, woodland gardens, entrance planting and evergreen structure.

visual: Dense evergreen shrub with small glossy dark green leaves and an exceptional spring display of rich cobalt to deep blue flower clusters opening from reddish-purple buds.
water: Water regularly while establishing, then reduce irrigation once well rooted.
soil: Free-draining, any pH; Winter wet is the main killer
prune: Lightly trim immediately after flowering if necessary. Avoid cutting hard into old leafless wood because regeneration can be poor.
resilience: Fast and drought resistant once established, but ceanothus are not generally among the longest-lived shrubs and resent heavy pruning or waterlogged soil.
uses: Sunny walls, Mediterranean-style borders, pollinator planting, evergreen structure and blue-flowered specimen planting.

visual: Robust deciduous shrub with arching stems, peeling older bark and deeply coloured purple-black three-lobed foliage.
water: Water during establishment; mature plants are relatively tolerant of occasional drought.
soil: Any, moist, well-drained; Shallow chalk can cause chlorosis
prune: After flowering, remove selected older stems at the base where renewal is required. It also tolerates harder renovation if necessary.
resilience: One of the tougher dark-foliaged shrubs, tolerating cold, pruning and a broad range of soils with relatively few serious pest problems.
uses: Mixed shrub borders, dark foliage contrast, hedging, low-maintenance gardens and pollinator planting.

visual: Vigorous deciduous elder with exceptionally finely dissected purple-black foliage giving an acer-like lace effect.
water: Water while establishing. Once rooted it tolerates both relatively dry and fairly damp garden soils.
soil: Any ordinary garden soil; Rich ground makes it outgrow its space
prune: For the largest and darkest juvenile foliage, plants can be cut back hard in early spring.
resilience: Fast, vigorous and adaptable, tolerating substantial pruning and a wide range of ordinary garden conditions.
uses: Dark foliage contrast, mixed borders, wildlife planting, informal hedging and pollinator gardens.

visual: Compact rounded deciduous lilac with small dark green leaves and masses of fragrant lilac-pink flower panicles in late spring, packing classic lilac scent into a much smaller plant.
water: Water during establishment and during prolonged dry spells, particularly when grown in containers.
soil: Fertile; alkaline OK; Not wet ground or poor acid soil
prune: Remove faded flowerheads and lightly shape immediately after flowering if necessary. Avoid late-season pruning because it removes the following year's flower buds.
resilience: Compact, hardy and easy to maintain, with good tolerance of chalkier soils and urban conditions.
uses: Containers, small gardens, front gardens, scented planting, mixed borders and low informal hedges.

visual: Upright evergreen to semi-evergreen shrub carrying clusters of intensely fragrant pink-purple buds that open to pale pink and white flowers in the depths of winter, followed occasionally by dark berries.
water: Keep evenly moist while establishing and during prolonged drought, but never waterlog the roots.
soil: Humus-rich, well-drained; Will not forgive being moved
prune: Minimal pruning only. Remove dead or damaged shoots and make any essential shaping cuts immediately after flowering.
resilience: Long-lived when left undisturbed in suitable soil, but notably intolerant of transplanting, severe root disturbance and waterlogging.
uses: Winter gardens, scented planting, entrances, paths, sheltered shrub borders and courtyard planting.

visual: Dense evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and tiny creamy-white winter flowers that are visually modest but produce an extraordinarily strong sweet perfume, followed by shiny black berries.
water: Water during establishment; mature plants tolerate relatively dry shade but benefit from occasional deep watering during prolonged drought.
soil: Humus-rich, well-drained; Water in while establishing in dry shade
prune: Little pruning is needed; lightly trim after flowering or remove old congested stems if required.
resilience: Exceptionally useful in difficult shaded situations and tolerant of increasingly dry conditions once established.
uses: Dry shade, woodland planting, winter fragrance, evergreen ground structure, shaded containers and planting near paths or doors.

visual: Dense thorny deciduous shrub producing brilliant deep crimson flowers with conspicuous golden-yellow stamens on largely bare branches in early spring, followed by aromatic yellow-green quince-like fruits.
water: Water during establishment; mature plants are reasonably tolerant of dry spells.
soil: Any, reasonably drained; Thorny — keep clear of narrow paths
prune: After flowering, shorten side shoots where wall-trained and remove congested or poorly placed stems.
resilience: Extremely tough, adaptable and tolerant of pruning, urban conditions and a broad range of soils.
uses: Wall training, hedging, spring flowering, thorny boundary planting, pollinator gardens and fruit for preserves.

visual: Large arching deciduous shrub whose graceful stems become smothered in masses of soft pink bell-shaped flowers with yellow-marked throats in late spring and early summer.
water: Water well during establishment; established shrubs need extra water mainly during prolonged drought.
soil: Any, moist, well-drained; Give it width; clipping ruins the habit
prune: Immediately after flowering, remove some of the oldest flowered stems at the base to encourage replacement growth and retain an open arching structure.
resilience: Robust and easy to grow with few demanding requirements once established.
uses: Large shrub borders, cottage gardens, flowering screens, wildlife gardens and informal specimen planting.

visual: Low compact deciduous shrub forming a neat spreading mound of fresh green leaves, almost disappearing beneath masses of small pure white starry flowers in late spring before developing purplish autumn tones.
water: Water during establishment and prolonged dry spells.
soil: Any, moist, well-drained; Avoid waterlogging and dry poor soil
prune: If pruning is required, do it immediately after flowering and remove some older shoots at the base to encourage fresh flowering wood.
resilience: Dependable, hardy and relatively trouble-free, needing little intervention once established.
uses: Front of borders, small gardens, low flowering shrubs, containers and cottage gardens.

visual: Bushy deciduous shrub with lobed aromatic foliage and hanging clusters of rich crimson-red flowers in early spring, later sometimes followed by rounded blue-black fruits with a pale bloom.
water: Water during establishment; mature plants tolerate ordinary seasonal dry periods.
soil: Any, reasonably drained; Pungent foliage when handled
prune: After flowering, remove a proportion of older stems at ground level where renewal is needed and lightly shorten overlong shoots.
resilience: Tough, adaptable and reliable, with excellent early-season flowering even in relatively ordinary garden conditions.
uses: Early pollinator planting, mixed hedges, shrub borders, informal screens and cottage gardens.

visual: Dense evergreen shrub with large glossy leathery leaves dramatically splashed and spotted yellow-gold.
water: Water regularly while establishing; mature plants tolerate dry shade surprisingly well once rooted.
soil: Any, reasonably drained; Direct sun scorches the leaves
prune: Prune or renovate in spring if needed, cutting overgrown stems back individually rather than shearing the large leaves.
resilience: Exceptionally useful for shade, urban conditions and root competition once established, with very low routine maintenance.
uses: Deep shade, evergreen screening, difficult dry borders, containers and foliage planting.

visual: Slow-growing evergreen ericaceous shrub with glossy leaves and remarkable clusters of angular deep red flower buds opening into patterned pink cup-shaped flowers.
water: Keep evenly moist, especially during establishment and in containers.
soil: Humus-rich, ericaceous; Strictly lime-hating; roots resent moving
prune: Usually needs little pruning. Deadhead or lightly shape after flowering if required.
resilience: Cold tolerant and long-lived but slow growing, with poor tolerance of alkaline soil, drought and root disturbance.
uses: Ericaceous borders, woodland gardens, specimen shrubs, containers and unusual flowering displays.

visual: Elegant deciduous ericaceous shrub with a tiered branching habit and clusters of small waxy bell-shaped cream to pinkish flowers marked with red veins in late spring.
water: Keep evenly moist, particularly while establishing and during dry summer weather.
soil: Humus-rich, acid-neutral; Avoid chalk and prolonged drought
prune: Needs little regular pruning. Remove damaged, crossing or unwanted stems after flowering.
resilience: Long-lived and cold hardy once established, but less tolerant of alkaline soils and summer drought.
uses: Woodland gardens, autumn-colour planting, ericaceous borders, Japanese-style gardens and specimen planting.

visual: Slow-growing deciduous shrub with rounded blue-green leaves and fragrant white bottlebrush flower spikes appearing on bare or newly emerging branches in spring, followed by exceptional mixtures of yellow, orange, red and purple foliage in autumn.
water: Keep consistently moist during establishment and dry weather.
soil: Humus-rich, acid-neutral; Avoid chalk and prolonged drought
prune: Minimal pruning. Remove damaged or crossing branches after flowering if required.
resilience: Generally healthy and long-lived in suitable acid to neutral soil, though slow-growing and less tolerant of drought or lime.
uses: Autumn-colour gardens, ericaceous borders, woodland edges, specimen planting and large containers.

visual: Elegant deciduous tree valued above all for exceptionally bright white peeling bark, which becomes increasingly striking as the stems mature.
water: Water thoroughly during establishment and prolonged dry periods, particularly on light soils.
soil: Fertile, moist, drained; Not for drought or standing water
prune: Prune only when necessary, preferably in late summer or early autumn; birches can bleed heavily if cut in late winter or spring.
resilience: Cold hardy and adaptable, though young trees need adequate moisture while their root system establishes.
uses: Winter bark displays, multi-stem specimens, avenues, contemporary gardens and mixed tree planting.

visual: Graceful large shrub or small multi-stem tree with bronze young foliage unfolding alongside clouds of white spring blossom, followed by red-purple edible berries and a final display of fiery orange-red autumn colour.
water: Water during establishment and prolonged dry periods, especially on light soils.
soil: Moist, acid to neutral; Avoid shallow chalk and drought
prune: Little pruning is required. Remove dead, crossing or badly placed branches during dormancy and preserve the natural multi-stem form where possible.
resilience: Reliable, cold hardy and generally easy to establish where the soil is not strongly alkaline or drought-prone.
uses: Small gardens, multi-stem trees, wildlife planting, edible landscapes, spring blossom and autumn-colour schemes.

visual: Broad spreading deciduous tree or large multi-stem shrub with attractive flaking bark, curious clusters of crimson-red flowers appearing on bare branches in late winter, and foliage that can combine yellow, orange, scarlet and purple in autumn.
water: Water thoroughly while establishing; mature trees tolerate moderate summer dryness.
soil: Any drained; lime OK; Allow real width — it spreads broadly
prune: Requires little routine pruning. Remove damaged or badly placed branches while young to establish the desired framework.
resilience: Long-lived, hardy and tolerant of a broad range of soils including lime, with generally low maintenance requirements.
uses: Autumn colour, multi-stem specimens, small to medium trees, winter interest and chalk-tolerant ornamental planting.

visual: Elegant deciduous tupelo selected for extraordinary autumn colour, when glossy green leaves ignite through brilliant orange, scarlet and crimson on a broadly conical tree.
water: Keep reliably moist during establishment and in extended dry weather.
soil: Moist, acid to neutral; Lime intolerant; no chalk, no drought
prune: Minimal pruning. Remove damaged or poorly positioned branches while young to establish a balanced framework.
resilience: Cold tolerant and long-lived in acid, moisture-retentive soils but performs poorly on chalk or severely dry sites.
uses: Autumn-colour specimen tree, lawns, acid gardens, waterside planting and larger gardens.

visual: Slow-growing deciduous small tree renowned for smooth cinnamon-brown bark that peels away in thin translucent papery curls, particularly dramatic when backlit by low winter sun.
water: Water regularly during establishment and prolonged dry spells.
soil: Fertile, moist, drained; Avoid drought and waterlogging
prune: Prune only when necessary, preferably in late summer to minimise sap bleeding.
resilience: Long-lived and hardy once established but naturally slow growing, so major damage takes time to replace.
uses: Winter bark, autumn colour, specimen planting, small gardens and multi-season tree collections.

visual: Distinctive deciduous hazel with bizarrely twisted and corkscrewing branches, especially striking after leaf fall, plus hanging yellow catkins in late winter before the crumpled green foliage emerges.
water: Water during establishment; mature plants tolerate ordinary summer dry periods.
soil: Any, reasonably drained; If grafted, pull straight suckers early
prune: Remove any straight rootstock suckers completely at their origin. Otherwise prune minimally, removing damaged or badly positioned growth while dormant.
resilience: Robust and adaptable, with the principal maintenance issue being removal of vigorous straight rootstock suckers on grafted plants.
uses: Winter structure, cut stems, specimen shrubs, wildlife gardens, containers and architectural planting.

visual: Distinctive small to medium deciduous tree with large pinnate leaves, airy panicles of bright yellow flowers in high summer and inflated papery lantern-like seed capsules that mature through bronze and brown.
water: Water while establishing. Older trees tolerate relatively dry conditions once well rooted.
soil: Well-drained, any pH; Cold shade spoils flower and seed set
prune: Minimal pruning. Remove damaged or badly placed branches during dormancy and establish a sound framework when young.
resilience: Once established it tolerates heat, urban conditions and periods of drought well, though young trees are less forgiving of severe exposure.
uses: Small tree specimens, urban gardens, drought-tolerant planting, summer flowering and unusual seed displays.

visual: Elegant open-crowned deciduous tree with fine fern-like foliage emerging brilliant golden yellow, maturing to light green and colouring yellow again in autumn.
water: Water thoroughly while establishing; mature trees tolerate periods of drought.
soil: Any well-drained soil; A full tree — not a container plant
prune: Minimal pruning. Remove damaged or crossing branches while young and maintain a clear structural framework.
resilience: Tolerant of urban air, heat and a broad range of soils once established, although young growth can be affected by gall midge and other occasional pests.
uses: Urban trees, light-canopy shade, lawn specimens, modern gardens and golden-foliage planting.

visual: Compact, bushier selection of cider gum with striking silver-blue juvenile leaves and pale stems.
water: Water well during establishment; once rooted, plants tolerate moderate drought but respond to summer moisture with stronger growth.
soil: Fertile, drained, any pH; Still woody and large if left unpruned
prune: For juvenile cut foliage, coppice or pollard established plants in spring once frost risk has eased. Unpruned specimens can instead be trained as small trees.
resilience: Fast growing and strongly regenerative after pruning, with good cold tolerance for a eucalyptus but some vulnerability while newly planted.
uses: Silver foliage, cut foliage, specimen shrubs, small trees, contemporary planting and large containers with pruning.

visual: Powerful deciduous climber famous for extraordinarily long hanging racemes of fragrant lilac-violet pea flowers in late spring and early summer, often displayed most effectively from pergolas and high supports.
water: Water regularly while establishing and during dry periods, especially before and during flowering.
soil: Fertile, moist, drained; Needs a genuinely permanent support
prune: Prune twice yearly.
resilience: Extremely vigorous and long-lived when established, but flowering quality depends on adequate sun, mature grafted material and correct pruning.
uses: Pergolas, arches, large walls, trained climbers and spectacular spring flowering.

visual: Glossy evergreen woody climber with dark green oval leaves that often bronze or redden in cold weather, carrying masses of intensely fragrant white pinwheel-shaped flowers through summer.
water: Water regularly while establishing and keep containers consistently moist during warm weather.
soil: Humus-rich, free-draining; Cold exposure and winter wet set it back
prune: Trim after flowering to keep growth within bounds and remove congested or damaged stems. Tie young shoots to supports until the framework establishes.
resilience: Dependable evergreen climber in warm sheltered gardens and increasingly tolerant of dryness once established, but exposure is its main limitation.
uses: Evergreen climber, scented walls, fences, pergolas, courtyards and large containers.

visual: Vigorous self-clinging evergreen ivy with exceptionally large leathery dark green leaves dramatically splashed through the centre with yellow and lime-green variegation.
water: Water regularly while establishing; older plants tolerate considerable shade and moderate drought.
soil: Any fertile, drained soil; Keep off gutters, roofs and soft mortar
prune: Trim at almost any time to keep growth within its allotted area. Renovate overgrown plants progressively if necessary.
resilience: Exceptionally robust, shade tolerant and drought resistant once established, though vigorous growth demands active containment on structures.
uses: Evergreen wall cover, shade, screening, wildlife habitat, late nectar and large containers.

visual: Vigorous twining climber with elegant leaves divided into five leaflets and clusters of unusual dark maroon-purple spring flowers with a sweet vanilla-chocolate-like fragrance.
water: Water regularly during establishment and prolonged drought.
soil: Any fertile, moist soil; Will swamp small shrubs and weak trellis
prune: Prune after flowering to contain growth and remove tangled or congested stems. More substantial renovation can be carried out where necessary.
resilience: Fast, vigorous and broadly adaptable, with strong regenerative growth after pruning.
uses: Pergolas, fences, scented climbers, wildlife gardens and unusual fruit displays.

visual: Twining deciduous honeysuckle producing long tubular flowers that are deep reddish-purple outside and creamy yellow within, followed by red berries.
water: Keep evenly moist while establishing and during dry summers.
soil: Humus-rich, moist, any pH; Not for dry starved soil; needs support
prune: Lightly prune after flowering to control size. Old congested plants can be renovated more strongly in late winter.
resilience: Strong-growing and cold hardy, although mildew and aphids can become more troublesome during dry or congested conditions.
uses: Wildlife gardens, moth planting, pergolas, fences, cottage gardens and evening-scented planting.

visual: Vigorous spreading hardy geranium forming a broad mound of deeply divided green foliage covered for months in large violet-blue flowers with darker purple veins and a small pale centre.
water: Water during establishment and prolonged drought; established plants tolerate ordinary short dry periods.
soil: Any fertile, drained soil; Rich soil or shade makes it sprawl
prune: Shear or cut sprawling growth back during summer if needed; plants rapidly produce fresh foliage and another flush of flowers.
resilience: Long-flowering, hardy, vigorous and generally low maintenance, making it one of the most dependable modern hardy geraniums.
uses: Ground cover, borders, containers, cottage gardens, pollinator planting and long-season flowering.

visual: Bushy evergreen short-lived perennial with narrow grey-green leaves and upright racemes of purple-mauve flowers produced over an exceptionally long season, often from spring well into autumn and during mild winter spells.
water: Water while establishing; mature plants prefer relatively dry conditions and dislike constant irrigation.
soil: Well-drained, lean; Wet winter soil shortens its life
prune: Lightly trim after major flowering flushes to maintain a compact shape, but avoid hard pruning into old leafless woody stems.
resilience: Exceptionally floriferous but naturally relatively short-lived, often declining after a few years; easy replacement from cuttings is therefore useful.
uses: Pollinator planting, gravel gardens, sunny borders, coastal gardens and containers.

visual: Broad aromatic mound of soft grey-green foliage carrying masses of blue-violet flowers on branching stems from late spring through summer, with repeat flowering after cutting back.
water: Water while establishing; mature plants are drought tolerant once rooted.
soil: Well-drained, lean; Rich wet soil makes it flop
prune: Cut back after the first major flush of flowers to encourage fresh foliage and repeat bloom.
resilience: Hardy, drought tolerant, pollinator-friendly and generally very easy to maintain once established.
uses: Pollinator borders, path edging, cottage gardens, gravel planting, roses, containers and drought-tolerant schemes.

latin: Helleborus (Rodney Davey Marbled Group) Anna's Red ('Abcrd02')
visual: Clump-forming hellebore with leathery evergreen leaves intricately marbled cream and sometimes flushed pink when young.
water: Keep moderately moist and water during prolonged dry periods, especially in containers.
soil: Fertile, moist, drained; No winter standing water at the crown
prune: Remove old, damaged or badly spotted foliage in late winter as flower stems emerge, but retain healthy attractive marbled leaves.
resilience: Long-lived, cold hardy and shade tolerant where drainage is good, although hellebore leaf spot, aphids and slugs can occasionally affect appearance.
uses: Winter containers, woodland edges, shaded borders, winter-flowering displays and underplanting deciduous shrubs.

visual: Graceful deciduous ornamental grass forming cascading mounds of narrow arching golden-yellow leaves striped with green, moving fluidly in the breeze and often developing reddish autumn tints before dying back.
water: Keep consistently moist during active growth and water containers regularly in warm weather.
soil: Humus-rich, moist; Emerges very late — do not dig it up
prune: Leave the old foliage for winter protection and interest, then cut it close to ground level in late winter before new shoots begin emerging.
resilience: Long-lived and cold hardy where soil moisture is reliable, but growth is naturally slow to moderate and emergence is notably late in spring.
uses: Shade gardens, woodland edges, containers, path edging, Japanese-style planting and cascading over walls or raised beds.
